task: Composite mangrove risk index combining TC regime shifts and sea-level rise, applied globally to evaluate end-of-century mangrove and ecosystem-service risk.
named_inputs: Global Mangrove Watch v4 sample points (Bunting et al. 2018)
IPCC AR6 medium-confidence regional RSLR rates – SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5 (Garner et al. 2021)
MIT downscaled TC tracks from CMIP6 MPI-ESM1-2-HR historical (Emanuel et al. 2006)
UCSC Changing Wealth of Nations mangrove ES values per country (Risk_Pop, Risk_Stock, Ben_Pop, Ben_Stock for 1996/2010/2015/2020)
method_steps: 1. Compute baseline TC exposure per mangrove point as count of MIT historical track points >=33 m/s within 200 km, weighted by intensity to flag intense (Cat4-5) hazard.
2. Extract SLR median rate (quantile=0.5) at year 2090 (mid of 2080-2100 window) from each IPCC AR6 scenario at the nearest AR6 RSLR location.
3. Threshold each mangrove point against the Saintilan et al. 2023 RSLR adjustment limits (4, 7 mm/yr) and Mo et al. 2023 cyclone-intensity stratification.
4. Build composite risk index as weighted sum of standardized TC exposure (with intense-storm boost) and SLR rate exceedance, normalized to 0-1.
5. Aggregate point-wise risk to country level, link to UCSC ecosystem-service variables to estimate exposed populations and natural-capital stock at risk.
6. Compare across SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5 and produce figures and tables.
primary_outputs: outputs/mangrove_point_risk.csv (per point: lat, lon, country, TC exposure, SLR rate per scenario, composite risk per scenario)
outputs/country_risk_summary.csv (per country: mean risk, mangrove sample share at high risk, exposed population, exposed stock)
